authority: Resolve six missing-nutrient recipes; user explicitly permits replacing the unevidenced mirin seasoning in D069. No other ingredient or method changes.
basis: Per one complete serving; ingredient-input estimates, not laboratory measurements of cooked meals.

methodology.scaling: Use the current one-serving ingredient quantity directly, per100 basis in g or ml; never halve a one-serving quantity again. Sum unrounded contributions before display rounding.
methodology.unavailable: A missing source remains null and cannot contribute a zero or a complete total.
methodology.salt: Sum unrounded sodium mg, multiply by 2.5/1000.
methodology.trace: Retain reported Tr tokens. A computational zero for a documented source trace is at source precision, not a fabricated measured zero.
methodology.energy: Retain established source energy for unchanged ingredients. methodology.variability: Two Thai origins are averaged as in the prior carbohydrate reconciliation. Stalk/rhizome edible-portion composition is an estimate for the specified tender core/peeled rhizome; cultivar, trimming and cooking vary. before.name: Lemongrass chicken noodle salad
before.description: Lemongrass chicken with rice noodles, crisp vegetables, fresh herbs and a lime and fish sauce dressing.
before.equipment: 0.1 g kitchen scales; knife and board; mixing bowls; pans or trays specified in method; clean food probe; metal skewers or steamer where specified

ingredients.quantity: 10 g (chicken; raw edible core finely minced)

method: Weigh the ingredients for one serving before starting. Keep any amounts for the dough, filling and sauce separate so that each goes into the correct part of the recipe.

Remove tough lemongrass layers before weighing the tender core. Mince extremely finely with garlic, then mix with the chicken fish sauce, sugar and oil. Flatten thigh pieces and marinate refrigerated for 30 minutes. Use the listed herbs, spices or citrus for flavour before considering any extra seasoning.

Soak or cook rice noodles in 750 g boiling process water according to their width, about 3-6 minutes; drain and cool. Keep the heat low enough that the rice cooks steadily rather than boiling over. At the end, check that a grain is tender right through, then let the rice rest as directed before loosening it with a fork. Separate the pasta or noodles as they soften so they do not stick together.
Check the texture towards the end of the cooking time; it should be tender with no chalky centre. No leaching reduction is applied to the dry noodle input estimate.

Cut cucumber and carrot into fine batons and thinly slice shallot. Keep the pieces a similar size so they cook evenly. Keep any ingredients that are added later separate from those that go into the pan first. Mix every dressing ingredient until sugar dissolves. Mix until the added ingredients are evenly distributed. Scrape around the sides of the bowl or pan as appropriate, so the measured mixture is used throughout the serving. Tear mint and coriander leaves.

Griddle chicken over medium-high heat for 6-8 minutes per side until the poultry endpoint is met. Simmer all leftover marinade and collected chicken juices to a safe bubbling finish. Look for small, gentle bubbles rather than a rolling boil. Stir along the bottom when needed to prevent sticking, and keep the heat low enough for the food to cook evenly.

Slice chicken. Toss noodles, vegetables and herbs with the complete dressing; top with chicken and cooked marinade. Check the thickest piece with a clean food thermometer: the centre should reach 75°C for at least 30 seconds. Check more than one piece if their sizes differ, and use clean utensils for the cooked food. Serve the whole salad as one serving. Thai-style lime, chilli and fish-sauce dressing is distinct from Indonesian peanut-tamarind satay.
Check the centre of the meat with a clean food thermometer: it should reach 75°C for at least 30 seconds. Do not wash raw poultry, and use clean utensils for the cooked food.

before.name: Bánh mì-inspired chicken baguette
before.description: A crusty baguette filled with lemongrass chicken, pickled carrot and mooli, cucumber, coriander and mayonnaise.
before.equipment: 0.1 g kitchen scales; knife and board; mixing bowls; pans or trays specified in method; clean food probe; metal skewers or steamer where specified

ingredients.quantity: 7.5 g (chicken; raw edible core finely minced)
17.5 g (quick pickle; as sold, weighed grams)

method: Weigh the ingredients for one serving before starting. Keep any amounts for the dough, filling and sauce separate so that each goes into the correct part of the recipe.

Finely mince the tender lemongrass core and garlic. Combine chicken marinade ingredients and refrigerate flattened thigh meat in them for 30 minutes. Cover and keep chilled while you prepare the other parts of the recipe. Keep raw meat and its utensils separate from ready-to-eat salad and cooked food.

Julienne carrot and mooli. Toss with the pickle vinegar, water, sugar and salt in a shallow bowl for 30 minutes. This is a small fresh pickle salad, not a preserved jar. Reserve all its liquor for serving.

Roast chicken and all marinade in a small rimmed dish at 220 C conventional or 200 C fan for 20-25 minutes, checking the poultry endpoint. Check the thickest piece with a clean food thermometer: the centre should reach 75°C for at least 30 seconds. Check more than one piece if their sizes differ, and use clean utensils for the cooked food. Rest 3 minutes and slice; safely simmer any thin juices if needed. Look for small, gentle bubbles rather than a rolling boil. Stir along the bottom when needed to prevent sticking, and keep the heat low enough for the food to cook evenly. Use the measured seasoning and sauces shown in the ingredients; do not add extra salt or a potassium-based salt substitute.
Warm the 120 g baguette portion and split it lengthways. Spread mayonnaise inside, then layer cucumber, chicken with cooked juices, pickle vegetables, coriander and finely sliced chilli.

Serve all the pickle liquor as a small side dressing for this serving so the measured sugar, vinegar and salt remain part of the eaten specification. Omitting or draining it requires a revised nutrition calculation.
Check the centre of the meat with a clean food thermometer: it should reach 75°C for at least 30 seconds. Do not wash raw poultry, and use clean utensils for the cooked food.

before.name: Chicken teriyaki-style rice bowl
before.description: Pan-seared chicken in a glossy soy and mirin-style glaze, served with rice, cucumber, carrot and sesame seeds.
before.equipment: 0.1 g kitchen scales; knife and board; mixing bowls; pans or trays specified in method; clean food probe; metal skewers or steamer where specified
method: Weigh the ingredients for one serving before starting. Keep any amounts for the dough, filling and sauce separate so that each goes into the correct part of the recipe.

Cook the rice component in its measured water, oil and salt in a close-fitting saucepan: bring to a simmer, cover on the lowest heat for 12-15 minutes, then rest off the heat for 10 minutes. Keep the heat low enough that the rice cooks steadily rather than boiling over. At the end, check that a grain is tender right through, then let the rice rest as directed before loosening it with a fork. Do not drain. Keep the complete cooked rice for this serving.

Use the specified Kikkoman mirin-style sweet seasoning measured as 17.5 ml, not 17.5 g. Its published nutrition is per 100 ml; no density conversion is invented. Mix with soy, sugar and sauce water. Use the measured seasoning and sauces shown in the ingredients; do not add extra salt or a potassium-based salt substitute.

Flatten thighs to an even thickness. Heat chicken oil in a non-stick pan, sear 5-6 minutes per side, then cover briefly until safely cooked. Let the pan warm before the food goes in. If the oil begins to smoke or the food catches immediately, lower the heat before continuing. Check the thickest piece with a clean food thermometer: the centre should reach 75°C for at least 30 seconds. Check more than one piece if their sizes differ, and use clean utensils for the cooked food. Keep the pan juices.

Add the teriyaki mixture and simmer, turning chicken repeatedly, for 3-5 minutes until glossy and clinging. Look for small, gentle bubbles rather than a rolling boil. Stir along the bottom when needed to prevent sticking, and keep the heat low enough for the food to cook evenly. Count all glaze; no alcohol-evaporation nutrient adjustment is claimed for this low-alcohol mirin-style product.

Toss finely cut cucumber and carrot with vinegar, sesame and sesame oil. Keep the pieces a similar size so they cook evenly. Keep any ingredients that are added later separate from those that go into the pan first. Slice the chicken and serve it with all the glaze, rice and side as one serving. Fibre, potassium and phosphorus for the exact mirin product remain unreported.
Check the centre of the meat with a clean food thermometer: it should reach 75°C for at least 30 seconds. Do not wash raw poultry, and use clean utensils for the cooked food.

before.name: Lemongrass pork with rice noodles
before.description: Lemongrass-marinated pork with rice noodles, crisp vegetables, fresh herbs and a lime dressing.
before.equipment: 0.1 g kitchen scales; knife and board; mixing bowls; pans or trays specified in method; clean food probe; metal skewers or steamer where specified

ingredients.item: Boneless pork shoulder, lean and edible fat
ingredients.shoppingItem: Boneless pork shoulder, lean and edible fat

ingredients.quantity: 14 g (pork; raw edible core finely minced)

method: Weigh the ingredients for one serving before starting. Keep any amounts for the dough, filling and sauce separate so that each goes into the correct part of the recipe.
Slice boneless pork shoulder across the grain 5 mm thick. Mince tender lemongrass core, garlic and shallot with the pork fish sauce, sugar, oil and pepper. Marinate pork refrigerated for 45 minutes.
Julienne carrot and mooli and toss with all dressing ingredients for 20 minutes as a fresh pickle dressing; no liquor is drained. Slice cucumber and tear mint and coriander.

Cook rice noodles in 900 g process water according to their packet, then drain and cool. Keep the heat low enough that the rice cooks steadily rather than boiling over. At the end, check that a grain is tender right through, then let the rice rest as directed before loosening it with a fork. Separate the pasta or noodles as they soften so they do not stick together.
Check the texture towards the end of the cooking time; it should be tender with no chalky centre. No numerical mineral leaching credit is applied.

Griddle pork in batches over medium-high heat for 3-5 minutes per side until safely cooked and browned. Simmer remaining marinade and collected juices until safely cooked before adding to the platter. Look for small, gentle bubbles rather than a rolling boil. Stir along the bottom when needed to prevent sticking, and keep the heat low enough for the food to cook evenly. Use the listed herbs, spices or citrus for flavour before considering any extra seasoning.
Serve all the noodles, pork and juices, vegetables, herbs and dressing in one large bowl.
Check the centre of the meat with a clean food thermometer: it should reach 75°C for at least 30 seconds.

before.description: Chicken and rice noodles in a coconut broth with lemongrass, galangal and chilli, finished with beansprouts and coriander.
before.equipment: 0.1 g kitchen scales; knife and board; mixing bowls; pans or trays specified in method; clean food probe; metal skewers or steamer where specified

ingredients.quantity: 12.5 g (laksa paste; raw edible core finely minced)
7.5 g (laksa paste; peeled raw edible rhizome)
17.5 g (laksa paste; as sold, weighed grams)

Finely mince peeled galangal, tender lemongrass core, garlic, shallot and chilli; pound with turmeric and coriander. Heat paste oil and fry the entire paste for 8-10 minutes until aromatic.

Add chicken cut into 2 cm pieces, all 325 g broth water and 75 g coconut milk. Simmer gently 15 minutes, then add remaining 100 g coconut milk, fish sauce and sugar. Look for small, gentle bubbles rather than a rolling boil. Stir along the bottom when needed to prevent sticking, and keep the heat low enough for the food to cook evenly. Continue 10 minutes until chicken is safely cooked. Use the listed herbs, spices or citrus for flavour before considering any extra seasoning.

Check the thickest piece with a clean food thermometer: the centre should reach 75°C for at least 30 seconds. Check more than one piece if their sizes differ, and use clean utensils for the cooked food. The chicken poaching liquor forms the stock and is retained.

Cook rice noodles in 900 g separate process water according to their packet; drain. Keep the heat low enough that the rice cooks steadily rather than boiling over. At the end, check that a grain is tender right through, then let the rice rest as directed before loosening it with a fork. Separate the pasta or noodles as they soften so they do not stick together. Check the texture towards the end of the cooking time; it should be tender with no chalky centre. Add beansprouts to the simmering broth for 3 minutes so they are thoroughly cooked.

Stir lime into the broth off the heat. Put all the noodles in one deep bowl, then add all the chicken, broth and coriander. This is a curry-laksa-inspired chicken version without an unquantified shrimp paste or stock cube.
Measure final served broth after kitchen testing to establish countable fluid per person; evaporation makes the 325 g input water an unsuitable final fluid claim.
